entries.title: New Swiss Liaison Prosecutor Flavia Roy starts at Eurojust

title_detail.value: New Swiss Liaison Prosecutor Flavia Roy starts at Eurojust

entries.summary: Flavia Roy has been appointed as the new Liaison Prosecutor for Switzerland. In her role, she will ensure that the Swiss authorities can work together with their counterparts from the EU on complex cross-border criminal investigations. She brings years of experience as a Public Prosecutor and Investigative Judge.

entries.title: EUR 1 million seized during ongoing investigation into money laundering network

title_detail.value: EUR 1 million seized during ongoing investigation into money laundering network

entries.summary: French and Italian authorities have continued to work together on an investigation into a money laundering network that uses gold bars to launder drug trafficking profits. Following an initial operation in which EUR 30 million was seized, criminal assets worth EUR 1 million were seized under the coordination of Eurojust and Europol, together with Kosovar authorities.

summary_detail.value: French and Italian authorities have continued to work together on an investigation into a money laundering network that uses gold bars to launder drug trafficking profits. Following an initial operation in which EUR 30 million was seized, criminal assets worth EUR 1 million were seized under the coordination of Eurojust and Europol, together with Kosovar authorities.

content.value: The international criminal network had set up a sophisticated money laundering scheme whereby the illicit proceeds generated from drug trafficking in France were collected at a residence in Italy and converted into gold bars and gold sheets. This made it possible to hide the illicit origin of the proceeds and transport them easily to other countries, in particular Kosovo*, Türkiye and Morocco. During the 10-month investigation, authorities found that at least EUR18million had been laundered.A couple is currently under investigation in Italy for orchestrating the money…

entries.summary: A Eurojust supported joint investigation team (JIT) between the Irish and Latvian authorities,and Europol, has led to Ireland's first convictions for human trafficking for the purpose of labour exploitation. Following the investigation, Irish courts sentenced two individuals to 13 and 11 years' imprisonment for offences including human trafficking, money laundering and forgery.

summary_detail.value: A Eurojust supported joint investigation team (JIT) between the Irish and Latvian authorities,and Europol, has led to Ireland's first convictions for human trafficking for the purpose of labour exploitation. Following the investigation, Irish courts sentenced two individuals to 13 and 11 years' imprisonment for offences including human trafficking, money laundering and forgery.

content.value: The two individuals, who were residing in Ireland, pleaded guilty to offences including human trafficking, money laundering and forgery committed between December 2020 and October 2023. They exploited seven victims who had been deceptively recruited from Latvia.The victims—six men and one woman, aged between 40 and 60—were lured to Ireland with promises of secure employment, good working conditions and accommodation. Instead, they were subjected to severe labour exploitation, resulting in physical and psychological harm and the theft of approximately EUR 750 000 in wages.During the trial, the…

entries.title: Eurojust and The Netherlands sign amended seat agreement

title_detail.value: Eurojust and The Netherlands sign amended seat agreement

entries.summary: Eurojust and the Dutch government have signed an amendment to the Agency’s seat agreement, further strengthening the framework for international judicial cooperation from Eurojust’s headquarters in The Hague. The amendment supports Eurojust’s growing cooperation with countries outside the European Union, including through liaison prosecutors seconded to the Agency. These prosecutors work side by side with their EU counterparts at Eurojust, helping national authorities coordinate swiftly and effectively in serious cross-border crime cases.

summary_detail.value: Eurojust and the Dutch government have signed an amendment to the Agency’s seat agreement, further strengthening the framework for international judicial cooperation from Eurojust’s headquarters in The Hague. The amendment supports Eurojust’s growing cooperation with countries outside the European Union, including through liaison prosecutors seconded to the Agency. These prosecutors work side by side with their EU counterparts at Eurojust, helping national authorities coordinate swiftly and effectively in serious cross-border crime cases.

content.value: Cooperation with third countries is becoming increasingly important to Eurojust’s work. Around 10% of the Agency’s cases already involve a country outside the European Union, underlining the fact that keeping Europe safe increasingly requires judicial cooperation beyond EU borders. Eurojust expects to welcome more liaison prosecutors in the coming years, further reinforcing The Hague as a hub for international criminal justice cooperation.The amended Seat Agreement was signed by Eurojust President Michael Schmid and Secretary-General of the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs Christiaan…

entries.summary: The seventh EuroMed Prosecutors General Forum offered a platform to strengthen cooperation between South Partner Countries, European Union Member States and Eurojust. title_detail.value: Eurojust handles close to 14 000 cases in 2025: Annual Report now live!

entries.summary: Discover Online ReportAs an integral part of the EU’s security and criminal justice architecture, Eurojust continues to increase its operational output, coordinating a record number of cases in 2025. The Eurojust Annual Report 2025 showcases the operational achievements of the agency including its growing number of casework, expanding global partnerships and expertise as the eminent EU hub for judicial cooperation.

content.value: Operational OutcomesIn 2025, Eurojust delivered a significant operational impact in the fight against cross-border crime. The Agency supported 13 946 criminal investigations, including 5 582 newly registered cases, and facilitated a record 412 joint investigation teams—nearly half of which also benefited from Eurojust funding totalling over EUR 2 million.Eurojust’s efforts contributed to the arrest or surrender of more than 4 443 suspects and the seizure or freezing of criminal assets valued at approximately EUR 1.2 billion.
